parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional household survey with multivariable regression analysis
parsed.population_and_sample: 256 residents of randomly sampled households in Mingo and Wyoming Counties, West Virginia; 42% response rate
parsed.exposure: Trust in the local water-treatment facility and its compliance with water-quality standards, alongside perceived tap-water quality, drinking-water problem salience, watershed pollution risks, income, and public-versus-private water supply
parsed.outcome: Household purchase of bottled or distilled water as a substitute for tap water, measured on a five-point agreement scale
parsed.rationale: The Methods and Measures sections (pp. 512–514) describe a household survey with an identifiable sample, institutional exposure—trust in the water-treatment facility—and an outcome measuring bottled-water purchase when residents do not rely on tap water. The Findings and Discussion (pp. 514–518) report regression evidence that distrust in the treatment facility, perceived tap-water quality, water-problem salience, and income predict this household coping behavior, making the study relevant to reliable and affordable drinking-water service access.
